3/18/26 3:00 PM Update:  We will be operating tomorrow, 3/19, with limited lifts and terrain: Chinook, Forest Queen, and Discovery will operate as scheduled, as well as Gold Hills + Quicksilver. Due to increased avalanche hazards the upper mountain will be closed. This includes Chair 6, Rainier Express, Green Valley, Quicksilver, Gold Hills and the Gondola (including Scenic Gondola.)  As a reminder, night skiing is done for the season.

Good afternoon skiers and riders! Today we have experienced off and on precipitation and some sun breaks through out the day. The groomers are riding very well with the soft spring like conditions!  Be aware of deep snow hazards: Ski and ride with a partner, keep them in sight, and have a plan to check in. Always ski and ride in control. Read up on Tree Well Safety here. Obey all closures and do not duck ropes.

Terrain Parks: Sudden Drop Park is open. Discovery Park and Arwine's Jump Line will be closed. 

Events:

This Week 
  • Toyota Free Ski Thursday is tomorrow! Drive your Toyota, Scion, or Lexus vehicle to Crystal Mountain on March 19, and grab one free lift ticket for the day. See Full details here. 
  • Happy Hour at Rafters Friday March 20th from 3-5pm.  
  • Pride in the Pow is this weekend March 21st-22nd. Join us for a full-on celebration of love, diversity, and good vibes. Whether you're carving up the slopes, busting a move on the dance floor, or enjoying the incredible drag performances, we've got something for everyone!
  • Summit Apres MTN Pride: Wrap up your mountain adventure in true Pride style at the Summit Après Party. Happening from 3-5PM March 21st at the Summit House, the highest-elevation celebration! 
Next Week
  • Intro to Backcountry Touring: March 27th, 28th, and 29th learn the essentials of backcountry travel in a beginner-friendly setting in this three-hour clinic. 
  • Nachtspektakel: On March 28th from 4-9PM tour under the stars indulge in tasty food & drink, hang out around the fire, and revel with other like-minded individuals. Then slide down the mountain in complete darkness, guided only by the stars and your headlamp!
Notes for today:
  1. $199 Spring 3-Day Passes are on sale now! Ski for just $67 a day, any day of the week, for the rest of the season!
  2. Looking to save time and make the most of the day? Consider grabbing a Daily Reserve Upgrade! Available on weekends and holidays, this upgrade grants access to priority lift access, getting you on the lift quicker and fresh tracks faster
  3. Did you know it just takes 5 Days to be entered to win a 26/27 Ikon Pass? Track your days on the Ikon App and register for RIDE TO WIN
  4. Paid reservations can only be cancelled by emailing SP+ at  CrystalMtnParking@spplus.com with Reservation #, First Name, and Last Name. While you may not receive an immediate reply, the cancellation will be processed. The Crystal Mountain Contact Center cannot process these cancellations.
  5. In case of on-mountain emergency: Call 360-663-3064 or 911

Mountain Weather 3/18/2026 4:20pm 

Forecaster: Bradford Swanson
  
Synopsis:   
 A stationary ridge has asserted its dominance over the region, resulting in a steady stream of rain for the next few days. This abrupt shift from last week's cold temperatures is due to a massive high-pressure system centered over the Southern U.S., bringing triple-digit heat to parts of California and Nevada. Thankfully, our heat wave is not quite that extreme, but we will be hovering in the mid-40s at the summit for the next couple of days. Directly to the West of us, Mt. Rainier is expected to receive just under 2” of rain between now and Friday. Thanks to the blocking pattern of that gigantic chunk of earth, Crystal is likely only going to receive about half of that onslaught, around .75”-1.00” of rain. Don't let these numbers scare you, the on-piste skiing is actually quite fun right now!

Thursday Night:

12hr Precip: Lt. 25” rain

Extended:   
Friday afternoon is expected to be the strongest part of this rain event, but it will also mark the start of a steep cool-down. This cooldown is not expected to result in any snowfall. Still, it will be an important factor in regaining strength in our snowpack. Additionally, we may see strong winds on Friday as this pattern change begins. This is not the most powerful rain event to hit Crystal, but it will be a shock to our snowpack as we transition from cold, deep powder snow to a wet maritime snowpack. 

*Daily Summaries: 12hr period representing 4am-4pm or 4pm-4am data
*Freezing Elevation (ft): Approximate elevation above sea level where the air temperature reaches 32 degree F

Uphill Travel Update: See the above banner for the current status. Please visit guest services to get your 25/26 uphill travel card. This must be renewed free of charge for the season. Uphill travel may be prohibited at any time as mountain operations teams conduct avalanche mitigation. Refer to the "No Uphill Travel" lights around the base area and the Mountain Report page indicating the status of the designated route. These lights are located by the Gondola trail map, at the bottom of Chinook, at the bottom of Discovery, and at the top of the Quicksilver lift shack. For more information about uphill travel, please visit the uphill travel page.
